Q: How to move blocks in VSCode? A:

VSCode can do this, but you have to select instead of adding a cursor.* So:

  1. Select with Shift+Down/Up
    • (i.e. cursorDownSelect / cursorUpSelect)
    • The selection needs to include at least one character of the lines you're trying to move, so if you're selecting down and the cursor ends up at the start of a line, or selecting up starting from the start of a line, that line is not included in the selection. You can usually just end/start one line further down, respectively.
  2. Move lines with Alt+Down/Up
    • (i.e. editor.action.moveLinesDownAction / editor.action.moveLinesUpAction)

* Your description isn't totally clear, and there are no commands containing the words "block select" in the current version of VSCode (1.69.2), but from the gif, it looks like you're doing "Add Cursor Below" (editor.action.insertCursorBelow). FWIW, I was also used to doing it like that, coming from Atom.

P.S. I tried some similar techniques and found a bunch of bugs, like that sometimes multiple lines will move if you put multiple cursors, but they won't be the right ones. I might file a bug report and add the link here.

Q: Qt: Could not initialize OLE (error 80010106) - (libwkhtmltox.dll) on C# A:

Set attribute [STAThread] to the CreatePdf method.

You might still get the error on the console, but at least the PDF file will be created.

Q: How to show a pygame window with a tkinter window? A:

Python doesn't have built-in multitasking.
It would need to use threading, multiprecessing or async.

root.mainloop() runs event loop which waits for end of tkinter program (for closing tkinter's main window) and it blocks next lines of code - so PyGame can't run own event loop while mainLoop

It would need to run one of them in separate thread or process.

You may also try to use root.update() inside Pygame loop instead of root.mainloop() and this will force tkinter to run one even's loop and update its widgets in every Pygame's loop.

This allows to process Pygame events and tkinter events at the same time.

On some systems if Pygame doesn't runs event.get() then system thinks that program freezed (because it doesn't response for events) and it may kill it.

Minimal working code:

#import sys   # you don't even use it in code

import pygame  # PEP8: every `import` in separate line
# from pygame.locals import *  # PEP8: `import * is not preferred

import tkinter as tk  # PEP8: all imports at the beginning
#from tkinter import *  # PEP8: `import *` is not preferred

pygame.init()

DISPLAYSURF = pygame.display.set_mode((0, 0), pygame.FULLSCREEN)

root = tk.Tk()
root.geometry("250x100")
# root.title("uh idk what to type") # you don't have to set it if you don't know what to type

label = tk.Label(root, text="Hello World!!", font=("Arial", 24))
label.pack(padx=20, pady=20)

# root.mainloop()  # it blocks code and waits for end of tkinter program (

main_loop = True  # PEP8: `lower_case_names` for variables and functions

while main_loop:
    for event in pygame.event.get():
        if event.type == pygame.QUIT:
            main_loop = False
    pygame.display.update()
    root.update()  # force `tkinter` to run event loop and update widgets

pygame.quit()

PEP 8 -- Style Guide for Python Code

Q: Segmentation fault with tensorboard 1.14 A:

I just had the same problem, in my case my env had both torch and full tensorflow. PyTorch and TensorFlow bundle conflicting native libraries, and the conflict segfaults the whole kernel silently.

I removed tensorflow (to remove the torch/TF native library conflict) and worked.

Q: Sorting by AM/PM time A:

The error message "Invalid time string "12:00:00 AM"" indicates that BigQuery's CAST(ActivityTime AS time) function does not recognize the "AM/PM" format directly. BigQuery's TIME data type expects a 24-hour format (e.g., '13:00:00' for 1 PM) and doesn't inherently understand AM/PM designators within a CAST operation.

To correctly sort your data by time, including AM/PM, you need to first convert your ActivityTime string into a format that BigQuery can interpret as a valid timestamp or time, taking into account the AM/PM. You can achieve this using PARSE_TIME with a format specifier.

Here's how you can modify your query:

SELECT
    *
FROM
    `modern-ellipse-438015-c0.Bellabeat.HourlyCalories3-4`
ORDER BY
    Id,
    ActivityDate,
    PARSE_TIME('%I:%M:%S %p', ActivityTime)

Explanation of the fix:

  • PARSE_TIME('%I:%M:%S %p', ActivityTime):

    • PARSE_TIME is a BigQuery function that parses a string according to a specified format and converts it into a TIME data type.

    • '%I:%M:%S %p' is the format specifier:

      • %I: Represents the hour in a 12-hour clock (01-12).

      • %M: Represents the minute (00-59).

      • %S: Represents the second (00-59).

      • %p: Represents the AM/PM meridian indicator.

This will correctly interpret your "1:00:00 am" and "1:00:00 pm" strings, allowing BigQuery to sort them in the desired chronological order.

Q: How can I retrieve a module's path? A:

If you used pip, then you can call pip show, but you must call it using the specific Python interpreter that you are using. For example, these could all give different results:

python -m pip show numpy
python2.7 -m pip show numpy
python3 -m pip show numpy

Example output:

Location: /System/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/2.7/Extras/lib/python

Don't simply run pip show numpy, because there is no guarantee that it will be the same pip that different Python interpreters are calling.

Q: Should I be creating a virtual environment for each project? A:

It's good practice to create a venv for your project to containerise its dependencies. If you instead let different projects use the same global pip, you can end up with two conflicting packages which require different versions of the same dependency.

As others have said, it is easy with a venv to share dependencies (pip freeze > requirements.txt). Also, if you use pyinstaller, you may find that bundling in an environment with many unrelated packages floating around can bloat the executable size; thus a venv is preferrable for a clean build.

If you don't like the extra step of calling the activate script (e.g. .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1) every time, you can setup a shortcut or alias.
